chapters.title: Chapter 828: Perfection
paragraphs: One thing Kent didn’t understand was the fact that people like Lady Enzi hadn’t ascended to a higher world yet.
From what he saw over the past few days, there were many elders in the sect, all of whom were qualified to become big shots in the high worlds.
Someone like Lady Enzi had the means to become a terrifying cultivator in a High world, yet she was still in a medium world doing god knows what.
That just didn’t make sense to Kent, so he sought answers.
Of course, Kent also knew that not everything had to make sense and that everything had a reason. No matter how unreasonable something is, it has its reason.
One of the said reasons was about to be addressed by Lady Enzi, who never expected Kent to ask such a question.
She stared at Kent for a whole minute before answering.
"Do you know high worlds are not all equal? Just like this medium world, where we have some worlds with overpowered cultivators and rich resources, the high worlds are the same.
Of course, you can choose any to ascend to, but as a cultivator, one can only aim for a world filled with resources. Ultimately, it’s all about resources.
Even this sect has a connection to 14 high worlds, with one housing monstrous talents, the kind that you can start to comprehend. We have sent thousands away already.

However, we aren’t rushing to ascend because before we do, we want to attain some level of perfection, at least one that would allow us to have a chance to one day become big shots in the high worlds."
Kent was a little taken aback by such an explanation.
’That is just bullshit. Someone like you is clearly ready to take the high world by storm, why wait for perfection again?’ Kent said inwardly, not understanding anything.

"That just doesn’t make sense to me. Someone with your strength has a big shot at making it big in the high world. Though I don’t know much about high worlds, I know enough to know you are worthy to join them.
So why then wait to become more perfect before ascending?"
Lady Enzi smiled.
This, for a moment, distracted Kent, making him wonder if she was only smiling for him or if she did so on a regular basis.
So far, she had smiled more than five times since he had known her, and that wasn’t like someone with her looks and strength.

"The only reason you are saying that is because in this medium world, you think I am strong enough. However, in the High Worlds, if I want to grow stronger and swim in the pool of geniuses, I need to be five times the person I am now."
Kent raised his brow.
"Right now, we have connections to high worlds, but all of them except one are graded low. From what we know, the strength of a high world comes in four stages.
The first is low, where although they are strong, the chances of meeting more than three Spirit Lords in the entire world are next to none.
They are high worlds, alright, but the weakest of them all."
’Fedora falls in this category. They only have two Spirit Lords. However, they aren’t weak either, just one person from there can take over Sonox overnight.’
Kent immediately formed his own conclusion from what he had heard, and it all started to make sense in a way.
The question he asked started to gain an answer, one he hadn’t fully heard but knew was the case: why someone like Lady Enzi would remain in a medium world.

"The second category is a ’Legacy’ High World. Of course, we choose to give them these grades based on the power level. But these High worlds have more than a hundred Spirit Lords, millions of Spirit Sovereigns, and billions of Spirit Kings.
The last time I met someone from those worlds, I lost miserably.
As for the third, which is known as the Great High Worlds, there are hundreds of thousands of Spirit Lords and even dozens of cultivators at the Heavenly Ascension stage.
As for the Supreme High Worlds, you can only imagine.
I want to ascend to a Legacy or Great High World.
From what I know, it isn’t only hard to get into a Legacy High World from a low one, but it is extremely dangerous even to attempt going there when one’s strength doesn’t speak for them

If possible, I also want to have a chance to survive in a Great High World before ascending. You may not know, but newly ascended cultivators are picked on and ridiculed to the point that most unfortunate ones become slaves forever."
"I guess when you put it that way, things do come into perspective. However, I have to ask, how would you know you are qualified to get to this High world or that High world?" Kent asked.
"It is simple. To know you qualify to get to a Low High world, you must score a 50% success rate inside the Perfect Chamber.
Of course, it is not a requirement, but since getting to a high world is expensive, one had to be ready not to lose their lives the moment they ascend."
Kent raised his brow. "What is a Perfect Chamber?"
Lady Enzi smiled. "We have a divine treasure that measures one’s perfection level by allowing them to fight perfect versions of themselves.
You will face the version of you that is regarded as perfect by the standards of medium worlds. In other words, you will have to fight yourself, which has no flaws, weaknesses, or defects.
Only when you manage to defeat yourself can you know you have successfully reached the limit of this world.
And before you ask me, no, I am yet to reach the level worthy of a Legacy High world. My score 200 years ago is still less than 70%.
And on the record, 50% takes you to a Low High world, 70% to a Legacy High world, 90% to a Great High World, and lastly, 100% to a Supreme High World."
’Interesting. Fedora is clearly a Low High World, and Pyris, the world I went to using the pill world, is a Legacy High world.
But if they already have cultivators that can threaten my life, then what does that say for the Great and Supreme High worlds?’

Lady Enzi read Kent’s expression and smiled, "I know what you are thinking, and the answer is yes, you may be a genius here, but unless you become the perfect version of yourself here, you can’t compare to those in the High worlds."
⟦Okay, I think I have forgiven her for using sneaky means to pull master into 100 duels. Now, I think I like what she is selling.⟧
’You like what she is selling. Why?’

⟦Because the next major part of the master’s training was to create a perfect version of you. However, it seems I wouldn’t have to worry about that now since the master will be going through it soon enough.⟧

’I see. In any case, when Gaia wakes up, I will let her build a Perfect Chamber for me so I can use it more actively since this is a sect and getting access to such a treasure might be expensive and time-consuming.’
⟦I will let the master know when she wakes up.⟧
’Thank you.’
Kent didn’t want to jinx it, but learning something new and finally making sense of why the High worlds had seemed different in a way.
He sensed it. Fedora was a weak High World, and Pyris had beings that could kill him. Now, he knew there were two more, not forgetting, unique worlds where the danger would be next to unimaginable.
’I have a lot to do before ascending’
He looked at Lady Enzi, "I suppose you called me here for a reason."

You will face the version of you that is regarded as perfect by the standards of medium worlds.
In other words, you will have to fight yourself, which has no flaws, weaknesses, or defects.
Only when you manage to defeat yourself can you know you have successfully reached the limit of this world.
And before you ask me, no, I am yet to reach the level worthy of a Legacy High world.
My score 200 years ago is still less than 70%.
And on the record, 50% takes you to a Low High world, 70% to a Legacy High world, 90% to a Great High World, and lastly, 100% to a Supreme High World."
’Interesting.
Fedora is clearly a Low High World, and Pyris, the world I went to using the pill world, is a Legacy High world.
But if they already have cultivators that can threaten my life, then what does that say for the Great and Supreme High worlds?’

Lady Enzi read Kent’s expression and smiled, "I know what you are thinking, and the answer is yes, you may be a genius here, but unless you become the perfect version of yourself here, you can’t compare to those in the High worlds."
⟦Okay, I think I have forgiven her for using sneaky means to pull master into 100 duels.
Now, I think I like what she is selling.⟧
’You like what she is selling.
Why?’
⟦Because the next major part of the master’s training was to create a perfect version of you.
However, it seems I wouldn’t have to worry about that now since the master will be going through it soon enough.⟧
’I see.

In any case, when Gaia wakes up, I will let her build a Perfect Chamber for me so I can use it more actively since this is a sect and getting access to such a treasure might be expensive and time-consuming.’
⟦I will let the master know when she wakes up.⟧
’Thank you.’
Kent didn’t want to jinx it, but learning something new and finally making sense of why the High worlds had seemed different in a way.
He sensed it.
Fedora was a weak High World, and Pyris had beings that could kill him.
Now, he knew there were two more, not forgetting, unique worlds where the danger would be next to unimaginable.
’I have a lot to do before ascending’
He looked at Lady Enzi, "I suppose you called me here for a reason."

chapters.title: Chapter 829 - 100 vs 1 (1) [Bonus]
paragraphs: "How confident are you of winning all 100 battles you will be fighting?" Lady Enzi asked, and Kent smiled.
"Let’s just say even if all 100 of them team up, I can end them in under ten seconds."
Lady Enzi raised her brow, hearing Kent’s bold words. He sounded arrogant, but he is confident in his abilities.
"You do know the sect is no place for the weak, right? Most of the disciples you will be fighting are all battle-hardened warriors who have been on many dangerous missions.
They are in no way weaker than you are."
"I know, Lady Enzi, but I am not underestimating anyone; I am just confident in myself." There were no comments from Lady Enzi for a few minutes before she stood up and extended her hand.
A badge appeared in her hand. "This is an access badge to the Perfect Chamber. After the battle, take it with you to the Inner Sect. Use it as early as possible."
Kent nodded. "Does this mean you think I will win all battles?"
"I don’t, but I would be happy if you manage to pull through." She waved her hand, and the glass before them cracked open.
Before Kent could admire it, his body moved, and soon he was outside, hovering beside Lady Enzi as they slowly descended onto the stage where the battle would be happening.
The moment they appeared, everyone quieted down.
Kent saw the 100 disciples who would be fighting him standing not far from the stage. Some were staring at him with calm expressions, while others looked at him with eyes full of competitiveness.
Kent ignored them all and focused on the match that was about to start.
"Listen up," Lady Enzi said, getting right to business. She had no plans to waste too much time on the battle she knew would be over before she knew it.
"If all things go according to plan, the battles will be over in under an hour, considering each of you just needs to last 5 seconds on the stage.
Of course, if you manage to last for more than 5 seconds against him, I will give you a million Supreme Points like I promised, so all of you should do well to at least last 5 seconds."
With that, she flew off the stage, leaving only Kent, who counted his footsteps and found the position he would be standing at.

He did promise that the one who would be able to make him move would be allowed to name a pill, and he would make it for them. So he found a place, and he stood, ready to remain there until the last person fell.
"The rules are simple. Since this is a seconds-type duel, we choose this arena where death, no matter how grim, is temporary. This means you shouldn’t fear death, at least this one’s.
But that also means you are free to go for the kill if you have the chance. On that note, the first person should get on the stage."
A slim, dark elf wielding two daggers was the first to get on the stage. Perhaps hoping to scare Kent, he used his speed to appear on the stage in under a second.
"You overestimate yourself, human, and that is why you will fall to my blade today," the dark elf said, and Kent shook his head.
"I don’t know about you, but I can already see how you die," Kent smirked and then looked at the dark elf from head to toe. "I can see you stabbing yourself through the heart."
The dark elf didn’t say anything but readied himself for a good fight. Everyone watching fell quiet and waited for the battle to begin.
They wanted to see what kind of person Kent was to have the spine to challenge both the inner and outer sect.
After a few tense moments, Lady Enzi spoke.
"Begin."
*SHING*
The dark elf threw one of his daggers, aiming for Kent’s chest, the moment the command was given. The strength behind the throw was so much that it arrived before Kent the next moment.
However, instead of stabbing Kent, the dagger stopped mid-air, caught between Kent’s fingers.
’One second.’
The dark elf didn’t bother with the defeat of his dagger throw.

Instead, he moved and aimed to close the gap, using sheer force to knock Kent back at least. However, when he was 2 meters from Kent, he heard a command, and he couldn’t stop himself from obeying the command
"STOP!" Kent commanded, and he did.
*2 seconds*
"Stab yourself through the heart."
There was no hesitation as the dark elf stabbed himself through the heart. On the third second, his body reassembled on the outside.
Silence enveloped everyone.
They all remained rooted, unsure of what they had just seen.
In one second, a dagger was through; in the second, a command was given; and in the third, the opponent was dead.
Nothing felt real, yet there they were, staring at what had happened as it was presented. Kent commanded his opponent to kill himself, and he did.
"This... is my eyes deceiving me, or did he just command Rizzen to stab himself, and he obeyed?"
"No need to doubt your eyes, I saw the same thing."
"Damn, is that even legal?"
Murmurs spread, and everyone started coming up with their own theories. They could not wrap their minds around what they’d just seen.
Rizzen stood outside the stage with a confused expression. He didn’t know why he did what he did. However, he knew when Kent asked him to stab himself, without any hesitation, he obeyed.
’What the hell just happened to me?’
Lady Enzi raised her brow and called the next person.
This time, a dragon climbed the stage in his demi-dragon form, featuring his wings, tail, and horns, with dragon scales all over his body.
Kent looked at him and smiled. "Let me guess, you plan on taking to the skies and using delay tactics to wait out the five seconds."

As if reading his mind, Kent was spot on; the guy wanted to delay the time so that when Lady Enzi gave the command, he was already in the air, not daring to come near Kent so he could play with his mind like he did with the Dark Elf.
However, Kent just smiled and snapped his fingers.

"Giant fireballs." Up in the air, dozens of large fireballs appeared, filling the stage with intense heat. The dragon dude was immediately consumed by the fire, incinerating his form in under 3 seconds.
He also resembled, on the outside, a feeling of a chill running down their spine. The fireballs deactivated the next second, bursting into fireworks as if celebrating his win.
This time, Lady Enzi widened her eyes.
’That was a divine grade flame art, and to think he was able to activate it with a snap of his finger. Just how strong is his soul?’
Kent remained in the same spot he had chosen to stand, looking smugly at the two defeated disciples standing in stunned silence, unsure of how any of this was possible.
The dragon dude expected his body to at least withstand the fire for a few seconds, but before he could even feel anything, his body was consumed, and then he appeared outside the stage.
Nothing felt real.
However, that only worsened as more disciples began appearing on the stage. It was just five seconds, as most would say, but that was enough for Kent to show them what true strength looks like.

chapters.title: Chapter 830 - 100 vs 1 (2)
paragraphs: "This is just unbelievable. How can someone who hadn’t even formed his core yet be this strong?" A disciple asked, staring at Kent, who had just defeated the 79th disciple.
All 79 disciples fell in under 3 seconds, shocking everyone to the core.
Regardless of the method his opponents used, none managed to last more than three seconds.

Most tried to use their defenses to shield themselves from Kent, hoping that by the time he breaks through their defenses, the five seconds will pass. However, regardless of how hard they tried, he always ended the battle in under three seconds.
"I think he is comparable to a Core disciple at this point. I mean, even Gruden lost, someone who had already scored 65% in the Perfect Chamber."
"Does this mean when it comes to how firm their foundation is, Kent is already above them when he hadn’t even become a fully fledge core formation cultivator?"
"I guess so. From what I know, one’s true power is determined by how firm their foundation is, and so far, Kent has shown his strength."
"Makes me wonder just how many aspects of cultivation he had already started walking."

"Well, he managed to block Mountain Man’s hammer with his palm, so I say he is walking the body cultivation path, and considering no soul attack seems to have any effect on him, he is also a soul cultivator."
"Damn, if all this is inside one person’s body, then isn’t he already comparable to those freaks in the Celestial Gate Sect?"
Every disciple, regardless of how their initial take on Kent’s character was, has now started to see something new in him, and that alone was making them come to terms with many things.
"He is a monster."
Kent had just taken down the 8th disciple, and at this point, everyone had given up on the idea that he wouldn’t be able to win all 100 battles.
"Next," Lady Enzi said, and Princess Elowen walked to the stage. She held her bow in her hand, her body radiating cold flame as she locked gaze with Kent.
"Don’t worry, I won’t ask you to burn yourself with your own flame," Kent laughed, and Princess Elowen sighed in relief.
"Thank you," she said.
The majority of the battles he won were fought by Kent simply asking his opponents to inflict harm on themselves, defeating them using their own weapons and hands.
So hearing he wouldn’t do the same to her made her very happy. Of course, there is the part where she will be dying in under 5 seconds.
"Begin."
The moment the command was given, the entire stage froze as white flames crawled onto Kent’s body, snaking around, aiming to devour him.
However, Kent just smiled and unleashed his soul flame, unfreezing a major part of the stage. However, the next second, an arrow appeared and exploded before him, creating a mist.
This blocked Kent’s vision, which bought Princess Elowen another second, making it two. She used her smart to take two seconds from Kent.
"Smart girl," up in the air, Lady Enzi muttered, watching Princess Elowen now circling Kent at a speed several times faster than all the disciples who had faced Kent so far.
’Three seconds,’ she muttered, moving very fast. She is ready and has already prepared a clone skill, so the moment Knet attacks, she plans to use it.
However, just when the clock hit 4 seconds, her body stopped in her tracks.
Her body froze like a statue, and then she found herself on the outside.
Four seconds—that was how long it took her, but she couldn’t defeat Kent. She came close, but she couldn’t.

"What just happened? How did she go from running to appearing outside the stage?" Nobody understood how it happened, not even Lady Enzi, who was now looking confused, staring between Kent and Princess Elowen.
She saw Kent’s hand move, but she didn’t see what happened afterward. It was fast, very fast, but he saw his hand move; however, the intent behind it eluded her.
"Hahahahaha!" Suddenly, Old Sword appeared over the stage, stopping beside Lady Enzi, his laughter echoing all over the arena and beyond.
A second later, Lady Liora, the Pill Emperor, also appeared.
"Hahaha... what a monster." Among the many who witnessed Kent and Princess Elowen’s battle, he was the only one who knew and understood what happened.
"Kid, tell me, how old are you again?"
"What a monster," Old Sword repeated his words, amplifying his voice so all could hear. "To those still lost, what just happened is what we swordmen call Intent solidification.

Most of you know and have learned that sword intent is the feeling a swordsman or anyone imposes on the battlefield. It is the belief, will, and intention manifested like an aura on the battlefield. We swordsmen call it sword intent.
It is invisible but can be felt. This also means that it can’t be used physically to attack. It can only be used mentally, and to some extent, on the soul level.
However, that is common knowledge among every swordsman. However, when it comes to mastering true sword intent, one can master it to the point where they can weaponize it.
It requires a much deeper understanding of sword intent even to consider learning something as profound as Intent Solidification.
But if one succeeds, then their future as sword experts will only see upward leaps.

And Kent, just 21 years old, a mere sword grandmaster, has already reached a level in intent solidification that even I, a sword emperor, haven’t yet... though, seeing him now, I think I can master it soon enough.
Of course, what I am saying may sound like gibberish to you, so let me put it in simple terms for everyone to understand.
What Kent had achieved is something that, when made public, will turn him into a sage that swordsmen all over the 64 allied worlds will come to him for lessons.

Sword Emperors will line up for him to teach them, for believe it or not, among all 12 sword emperors in the Alliance, none has mastered the basic form of intent solidification, not even to the stage Kent has.
Kent here is a treasure, and all swordsmen must respect him."
Once again, there was silence everywhere, all eyes staring at Kent.
Many still didn’t understand what Old Sword had said; however, hearing him say Kent had mastered something that even he hadn’t yet was enough for them to see Kent in a new light.
Kent, on the other hand, stared at the old man and smiled, "Your sight is sharp, old man."

Kent spoke, using the tone that Jest, his swordsman past life, would use. And he was right to use it for it captured Old Sword’s attention, making him see Kent as a true swordsman instead of a 21-year-old brat.
"Age is just a number, boy."
"I know. But still, you may have made me too popular. I am someone who likes staying under the radar."
Old Sword smirked, "Then you shouldn’t have challenged the entire sect if you wanted to stay under the radar."
Kent shook his head, a smile on his face, "I guess you are right. In any case, I have yet to master the solidification of sword intent. But I am not far from achieving basic mastery.
However, at the moment, I don’t have much time for it since it doesn’t define one’s sword path, so I have a proposal."
"I am listening," Old Sword smiled, knowing things are taking shape.

"I will demonstrate it 19 more times, by then I am sure you will capture it. Then you will use your knowledge to develop it, and, well, after you have achieved basic mastery, you can teach who you want to."
"And what is your demand, boy?"
"Very simple, actually. I want to experience your sword realm just once."
Old Sword raised his brow, staring at Kent like he had seen a ghost. The demand was just unexpected.
"Correct me if I am wrong, but in exchange for demonstrating Intent Solidification, I will allow you to experience my sword realm just once..."
"Just once."
"Are you sure?"
"Very sure, old man."
"You have yourself a deal."

chapters.title: Chapter 831 - 100 vs 1 (3)
paragraphs: Old Sword sat down in the air, ready to watch all 19 moves Kent would be making using Intent Solidification.
As a swordsman, this was a moment he would kill for, and now that he had a chance, he didn’t want to waste it, even if the current intent Kent would be displaying was but an incomplete form of it.
’This is a win-win situation for me. He may think I have asked for little, but if he knew what I intended to look for in his Sword Realm, he might kowtow to me to become his master.’
Kent smiled.
The intent solidification was something Jest had been researching long before he began searching for a way to the immortal world.
He did manage to find something, but he didn’t put his all into it.
So, since Jest only managed to grasp an incomplete mastery, it meant Kent had not yet fully grasped it either.
In fact, Jest had barely scratched the surface. It was Kent who had actually managed to make some form of progress out of it.

So he wasn’t ready to dive into it when he hadn’t yet created the foundation for the two remaining sword techniques, so he could finally become a Sword Saint and get his task for the Sword Sage level.
His main objective now was to create the techniques, and if teaching what he knew to a Sword Emperor would get him closer to what he desired, then he was ready.
Lady Enzi continued to stare at Kent for a full minute before calling the next person, a Wolfkin. He looked like he had given up as he moved toward the stage.
But who could blame him?
As someone who was praised by a Sword Emperor, going against him was already a losing battle.
Kent saw his beaten expression and smiled.
"Chin up, buddy, at least you will be making it into the Inner Sect, that is a win in my book," Kent said, and the Wolfkin smiled weakly.
"I guess you are right. In that case, let’s have a good fight."
"That is the spirit." Kent locked his gaze on the wolf boy, and for a moment, he saw a killing intent locked on his body, but it vanished the next second.
’Well, I will be damned, this kid has rather good control over his killing intent. He must have killed his fair share of people.’
Kent didn’t appear to sense the intent and merely stood there.
"Begin."
HOWL
The wolf boy howled and dashed at Kent.

At that moment, Old Sword activated his sword gaze, locking it on every move Kent was about to make. To him, the speed at which the wolf boy had just moved was but a slow movement, so when Kent flicked his hand, he saw everything.
It was at that moment that he saw what had eluded him for centuries.
It was subtle.
Invisible to the naked eye.
Sharp and faster.
The intent in the air, thanks to his sword gaze, had become slightly visible. He saw how they moved and formed when Kent moved his hand.
He saw how they solidified, turning into a thin blade, one that was both formless and edgeless. However, while none of this should be possible, he saw it move and cut the wolf boy in half.
Then it vanished.
’I need to see it once more,’ Old Sword said, waiting for the next opponent to come.
When Kent handled the next disciple, he managed to capture more details.
He saw the formless form of the sword intent solidify. However, it wasn’t complete like a true blade should be.
But even so, it moved, sharpening as it moved through the air, cutting his opponent in half, who happened to be Princess Freya.
Her death was painless and instant.
One moment she was on the stage, the next she was on the outside.
The more attacks unleashed, the quicker Old Sword’s understanding expanded until the 18th person arrived. That was when his knowledge of intent Solidification clicked.
At the moment his understanding formed, Kent sensed a change in the air, which told him his job was done.
’With a mere basic master, it will be hard to use it to kill a swordsman with a robust sword intent successfully.
However, with calculated precision, one can easily use it to end battles. Unexpected attacks, ones that no one would expect, can be unleashed thanks to intent solidification.
Of course, if Jest’s theory is valid, then one day, with just intent, I can cleave through planets and pluck stars from the sky.’
Kent raised his head and looked at Old Sword, who smiled back at him.
To Kent, this was merely an exchange, but to Old Sword, this was what he had been looking for all these years.

Just like Lady Enzi, who had broken two limits, mastered five mythic-grade skills to perfection, and even went as far as rebuilding her foundation five times over the years, Old Sword had also been through many such things, but no matter what, he couldn’t just rise to 70% of his true potential.
Only the sect master had reached 70% and had already started planning to ascend. With this new knowledge, he soon realized he would also need to start preparing to ascend to a High world.
His target is a legacy world, just like all powerhouses currently aiming for 70% improvement of their true potential.
"Big brother, please take it easy on me." The last person to face Kent was, of course, Nyss, who stepped onto the stage with a weak smile on her face.
"I’ve been waiting for you to come, but you never did. Finally, you are here." Kent smiled, wanting to move from his spot and get close, but he didn’t.
Instead, he remained rooted to his spot and locked gaze with Nyss.
"Don’t burn me too. I hate fire," Nyss said, already planning on getting inside Kent’s mind. However, the chaos dragon remained calm, only smiling at her.
Lady Enzi saw what she was doing and just smiled, "Begin."
*SNAP*
The moment he gave the order, Kent snapped his fingers and the sky turned golden, instantly forming into a storm.
Nyss, who was about to move, suddenly felt her body sealed.
"How?"
She asked, not understanding how Kent sealed her. Kent, of course, didn’t mind her. Instead, using his mind, he raised her body up, and from the cloud, a lightning bolt fell, landing on her body.
It went through her body, making her spasm before tossing her out. Kent didn’t kill her; instead, he electrocuted her and tossed her out, causing the cheeky demon girl to scream in pain.
Kent remained smiling for a few seconds before Nyss suddenly shot up on her feet and lifted her hand. A dark flame appeared, bringing a shocked expression to her face.
Kent’s smile widened.
"How?" Nyss asked again, jumping onto the stage.
"I electrocuted you," Kent answered.
"But just how did that break the seal on my soul flame?"

"It’s just a Tier 11 seal; breaking it wasn’t too hard." Kent shrugged, looking like he didn’t care that he had just broken a Tier 11 seal, something many array masters are still struggling with. Of course, if Alina were around, she would have clapped for him.

One of the gifts she gave him before they separated was a way to break Tier 12 seals and below. And Kent, who had already sensed the seal on Nyss since the moment she touched him, had been planning on helping her.
But who would have thought his chance would come through a duel and even get a chance to electrocute the sneaky demoness who had been annoying in the past few days?
"That sneaky witch, I am going to enjoy killing her," Nyss said, her eyes completely black as her body exuded some of her killing intent.
Some who knew her character took a few steps back.
"Who do you want to kill?" Kent asked.
"My stepmother... She was the one who sealed my soul flame and had set me back several years."
Kent just chuckled, "Good luck then."
And just like that, the duel was over.

chapters.title: Chapter 832: I Hate Men
paragraphs: With the match over, every disciple started making their way out of the arena.
They had each witnessed a shocking display of strength, and that alone left them stunned.
Those who, for reasons unknown, disliked Kent had all seen his shocking display, and that woke something in them - Fear.
They all saw what Kent could do, and while it was shocking, that gave them the wake-up call to snap out of their hate and see reality.

The inner disciples, hoping he would never make it to the Inner Sect, were all left disappointed, while the outer disciples, with dreams of making it to the Inner Sect before him, were seething, knowing he and a few others had left them in the dust.
Not only has Kent gained the recognition of a Sword Emperor, but he has also earned so much that anyone would kill their best friends for.
First, he had become an inner disciple 14 days after joining the sect.
Second, he now has a chance to spend seven days inside the Spiritual Core pool. It is one of the places any disciple would kill to enter.

Those who have yet to refine their cores would not only be able to do so much faster, but someone like Kent will also be able to level up once or twice due to the abundance of spiritual qi in that region.
It is so rich that anyone would love to spend just a day there, using the energy to either refine their core or strengthen their foundations.
The third, Kent, now has two chances to ask Lady Enzi for help. That is something not even elders can brag about.
Fourth, he had secured a spot to participate in the upcoming selection trial for disciples representing the sect in the interplanetary competition.
That alone is enough for anyone to take pride in.

Not only has he entered a pool that only Core disciples swim in, but Lady Enzi planned on adding him to the main strike team, the ones that will start all battles for the sect, instead of merely being a substitute.
That is such a great honor, and Kent can feel it.
Then there is the part where he had earned 500,000 supreme points and had the chance to select his own cultivation peak once he got to the inner sect.
That alone is enough and worth the trouble of winning 100 duels.
As for a chance to view the True Sword Tablet, Kent was looking forward to it.
[Lady Enzi’s Glass Domain - Aftermath of the Duel]
Kent found himself back in the glass domain, facing Lady Enzi, just as before. However, this time, the air in the space looked calm, and it was more focused on him.

Lady Enzi has a few questions for him, and Kent knew these questions would be ones he had to answer carefully, considering he had shocked both Lady Enzi and Lady Liora, two of the most powerful elders in the entire sect.
They sat in silence for five good minutes before Lady Enzi spoke.
"Are you a body cultivator?"
"Yes. I am a diamond body cultivator."
"I see. That explains the fact that you were able to take on a power swing from a Silver body and not take even a step back."
Kent nodded. Thanks to his body reaching the diamond stage, he was able to raise his strength to the point where blocking a giant hammer with his bare hand wasn’t a struggle.
Of course, drinking the elixir that allowed him and his legion to temper their bones had also played a crucial role in enabling him to use his hand as a form of defense.
Lady Enzi was clearly shocked to hear his body cultivation stage, but she didn’t allow it to show on her face. Instead, she asked the second question.
"What about soul cultivation?"
"I am currently at Tier 13."
She raised her brow this time. ’Not only is he a diamond body cultivator, but he is also a Tier 13 soul cultivator. Just who is this kid?’
Even she, at the moment, had only recently reached Tier 14, something she had spent over 2,000 years working on.
However, Kent is but a 21-year-old level 4 core formation cultivator, and he had already reached Tier 13; that is just too much.
"One last question, how many limits have you broken so far?" This question seemed a little personal, because many wouldn’t casually reveal the number of limits broken.
In the high worlds, where most spend a great deal to break their limits, if a cultivator finds out one surpasses them, they tend to take it not so well.
The chances of stabbing their own friends in the back are very high.
So, telling one the number of limits broken is not a good idea. Even Vexthra, who is a goddess, out of habit, nearly didn’t tell Kent when he asked.
But even after painstakingly breaking 76 limits, making her a powerhouse as a true god, she wouldn’t just tell anyone the number of limits she had broken.
But Kent doesn’t care about those things.
"I have broken four limits."
This time, Lady Enzi’s expression switched from shock to respect, and it remained like that while she stared at Kent for another ten minutes.
"No wonder that old goat praised you like you are some kind of a sage."
Kent laughed, "Yeah, that was a little over the nose, but I guess his words weren’t that bad."
"I suppose. In any case, you are an impressive young man."
"Good for me, I guess. Being praised by a fairy such as yourself is a dream come true."
"Tch, no need to flatter me with your words, I hate men," Lady Enzi said with a smirk.
Kent also smiled, "What a coincidence, I hate men too. They are just too destructive." Kent’s smile turned into laughter, filling the glass domain.
"We haven’t even gotten to know each other better, but we have already found something we have in common. I say this is a good start."

"Stop daydreaming, brat. After today, you will not even have a chance to talk to me. I just brought you here to get a good understanding of your strength so I can make a good argument for you to the sect leader."
"If the Pill Emperor said this, I might have believed her, but I don’t believe you, Lady Enzi. I can tell you won’t be able to keep your hands away from me from now on." Kent smirked.

"You are not my disciple, and I only talk to my disciples, whom I happen to have one now. So I won’t have time to entertain you much longer. That said, hand me your sect badge, let me transfer the supreme points to you."
Kent did as he was told, and soon, he had received the five hundred thousand supreme points she promised.
"Is she a core disciple... your disciple?" Kent asked.
"No. I am yet to recruit her, but I think you already have a fair idea."
"I see. In that case, good knowing you. I will be sure to keep my eyes on you," Kent said before standing up, "And oh, if you need assistance with any pill, don’t forget to book my services."
"My friend is a Pill Emperor, so I will be fine."
"Fair point. In that case, I will be on my way now." The glass cracked open, and Kent vanished through it. When he was gone, Lady Enzi also vanished and appeared somewhere in the core sect.

chapters.title: Chapter 833: Selecting A Cultivation Peak
paragraphs: "I can’t believe we have become Inner disciples within 14 days of joining the sect," Norion said, sitting in a flying treasure as they were taken to the Inner section of the sect.
"I expected to stay in the outer sect for at least two years, but this is indeed unexpected." Arion seconded Norion’s words.
None of them indeed expected things to work out this way. However, the dreams they held in their hearts were fulfilled at a relatively fast pace.
Of course, it’s all thanks to Kent, whose challenge has paved the way for them.
Kent was seated on the side, growing annoyed by Nyss, who had been bothering him for the past two days to spar with her.
Kent, of course, rejected all the attempts she made, and because she didn’t have enough Supreme Points to challenge him officially, she could only pester him.
"Big brother, you really are wicked. I even offered to cook for you for a single spar, but you rejected it. Do you know how many would beg me to offer them half of what I offered you?"
Kent looked at her and smirked, "I am not going to spar with you, so stop bothering me."
"Why, are you scared?" Nyss asked.
"Yes. I am scared for my life, so I won’t accept your challenge," Kent said with a slight chuckle at the end.𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
Nyss pouted, acting spoiled.
After Kent broke the seal on her body, she became even more powerful, surpassing even the other two geniuses. However, even so, she is still not at a level worthy of challenging a monster like Kent.
"The moment I get enough Supreme Points, I will challenge you... officially. You won’t be able to reject me then."
"I will reject you and pay the fine. Remember, I have 500,000 Supreme Points and I plan on using them to ensure your wishes never come through."
Kent laughed.
Teasing Nyss has become something he seems to enjoy these days, so he was making sure he teased her to his heart’s content.
It took a couple of minutes, but eventually, they arrived at the Inner Sect.
The first thing they saw was a series of towering mountains, about eight of them positioned strategically. Each mountain is bigger and taller.
Gazing at them, Kent could sense some powerful presence atop every last mountain. This presence doesn’t pale in comparison to Lady Enzi or Old Sword.
He also sensed some natural phenomena happening on the mountains. On one mountain, he sensed infernal energy radiating off it.
On the other mountain, he sensed lightning, and on the third mountain, he sensed the feeling of ice.
As they slowly moved, Kent paid more attention to the mountains. He counted eight, and after moving several hundred miles, he spotted another.
However, this one didn’t have any natural energy radiating off it. It stood tall, half of it broken, and there was no powerful presence located there.
It was just a normal mountain.
This caught Kent’s attention, so he continued to observe it. After a while, they finally came to a stop in front of an ample space with nothing but stone everywhere.
He looked up and saw that they had arrived at the center of the Inner Sect, where several disciples could be seen going about their daily business.
The place was so large that Kent’s senses couldn’t cover even half of it.
He tried, but he just couldn’t.
However, he counted many smaller training grounds, several stores, and many more amenities that he found fascinating.
"This place is cool," Kent said.
Watching the Inner disciples fly about, some on cloud horses and others on various mounts, his eyes lit up. The sect dream was all over him now, and he most certainly wanted to live it.
"Welcome to the inner section of the Supreme Immortal Sect," the elder who came for them said, allowing them to take in his words.
"You are currently in the Mutual Space, where all disciples from the various cultivation peaks come to interact with each other.
I know some of you have already managed to pick up a few things, but to those who haven’t, look closely at the badges on the chest of the disciples."

The answer is no. Joining any cultivation Peak is acceptable, as most of what happens there is determined by how resourceful you are.
If you are a swordsman and you have a flame element, you will be taught how to harness the flame into your swordsmanship.
All Peaks have departments for all forms of professions.
Of course, joining the Flame Peak means you will primarily deal with things related to flames. However, if you feel like your flame isn’t suited for the path you want to walk, you can switch peaks.
However, you have only a month to make that decision. Afterwards, you won’t be able to change it again.
Additionally, please note that resources are allocated based on your ranking on the Peak you choose, so it is always advisable to improve your ranking.
As to how to raise your ranking, you already know.

"That is the Abandoned Mountain. It used to be a cultivation peak, but as its name suggests, it is abandoned and doesn’t have a master, so nobody has joined it since the last time I can remember."

chapters.title: Chapter 834: Abandoned Mountain [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Grand Hall - Inner Sect]
Words that Kent had picked, the abandoned mountain as his cultivation peak, spread like wildfire, even finding its way to the core disciples.
The elders, regardless of their take on Kent’s recent performance, were all taken aback.
"Just what was he thinking by picking that place as his cultivation peak?" Elder Mikko asked, sitting in the Grand Hall with the other elders and Grand Elder Esper.
"You are asking the wrong people, Elder Mikko. Why don’t you direct this question to Kent himself? I am sure we all need to know why he chose that place."
Elder Mikko glared at the elder who spoke, but she didn’t say anything.
They all looked confused when the news of Kent’s decision reached them.
"What did Lady Enzi say about his decision?"
"She said nothing. Right after she chose that half-elf as her disciple, she went back to her dwelling and hasn’t come out yet.
Old Sword is also in seclusion, and as the only two people to have interacted with Kent the most, none of us know what to do."
"This is just too much. We have to do something before the sect leader finds out we have allowed such a promising disciple to pick such a place as his cultivation peak."
While the elders were trying to understand Kent’s decision, the disciples were also having a difficult time adapting to Kent’s sudden decision.

"I was looking forward to seeing him at the Flame Peak and perhaps getting some pointers from him, but now that he has picked such a place, my wishes won’t come true." A disciple said with a frown and a beaten expression.
"I heard rumors that something dark is hidden within that mountain." Another disciple said.
As usual, the disciples will add a unique twist to their words to make them sound more believable.

"Why are you complaining? I say this is good for us. With him out of the way, we will have a chance to compete for more resources. Imagine Kent joining the Flame Peak; he would have won all the resources from us."
"That is indeed true. This is for the best."
"Idiots. You and I both know that one Cultivation Peak can challenge another for resources. What if he challenges us? Imagine how much he will be making off our defeat."
"Oh, come on, Mark, you are making it sound like he alone can defeat a thousand of us."

"And you think he can’t? He had just defeated 100 of our finest, and that all happened in under an hour, all 100 of them defeated in under an hour. If that doesn’t say enough, then I don’t know what would."
"Shit, I forgot about that."𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
[Base of the Abandoned Mountain - Inner Sect]
While talks about Kent continued to spread everywhere, the man in question was now standing at the base of the abandoned mountain, looking up at the looming peak before him.
He could fly up, but Kent wanted to climb and see what kind of place he had chosen to spend the next few months at.
Of course, to many, what Kent had done was stupid. However, Kent made this decision for his own good.
First, he wanted to be able to slip in and out of the tower without prying eyes everywhere.
Although his plans to live the sect life were now taking shape, he also knew he had to continue training, and the only way to speed up the process was to use the tower, where time runs much faster.
So, while entering the tower for just a month would be equivalent to almost two years on the outside, he didn’t want people to notice his absence easily.
The second was a feeling he got from the mountain the moment he saw it.
It was strange and familiar in a way.
It was like he had sensed it before, and that was why he chose the abandoned mountain as his cultivation peak to investigate this feeling.
"Now standing here, I can sense it even more. I wonder what will make me this giddy."
To Kent, the resources the sect was offering could be obtained from the tower at a much cheaper rate, but the feeling couldn’t be bought.
So he was chasing after it.
He moved and started climbing.
"Tower, be sure to keep scanning and immediately prompt when you find something good."
⟦I will master⟧
Thus, Kent slowly started ascending the mountain.

He knew all this might pan out to be a giant waste of time, but he knew if he didn’t follow his feelings, he wouldn’t be able to rest, so he was steadily looking toward the main goal instead of the instant when he might come out looking like an idiot.
Four hours later, Kent was only 25% up the mountain.
The feeling was still there, so he wasn’t turning back.
His pal, the tower, was also scanning, giving him all the changes it was sensing.
After another four hours, Kent stopped and sat on a stone overlooking the vast and beautiful land that stretched far into the distance.
"This place is indeed beautiful. I will borrow some of their designs and incorporate them into my tower." Having a few towering mountains isn’t bad at all.
⟦The master shouldn’t worry. I have a complete architecture of the sect ready. With a few tweaks, you can implement it⟧
"You are the best, Tower," Kent smiled and remained on the stone for a couple of minutes before resuming the climb.
A few hours later, something new changed, and both Kent and the tower sensed it.
"That is a sword energy."
⟦There is sword energy in the air, master. Though faint, I can sense it⟧
"I do too, Tower, and it leads up the mountain. I’d better hurry up." Thus, Kent started climbing up the mountain much faster this time.

The change in the air was enough to tell him he wasn’t wasting his time. However, regardless of what he thought, he first needed to identify the root cause of the situation before he could make a decision.

Barely under 45 minutes, Kent was deep into the clouds, nearing the peak of the mountain. He could still sense the sword energy, but while he expected to feel a more concentrated form of it as he drew close to the source, nothing changed.
So Kent couldn’t get close to it any faster.

Eventually, he arrived at the peak of the mountain, which, from what greeted him, was a plain field of dried grass. It was vast, but aside from a large flat stone standing at the center of it, there was nothing else.
The only saving grace was that, along the mountain, there were some caves, and from what the tower managed to gather from them, a few still had functional cultivation formations.
So he knew he could use them.
However, with all the rushing and nearly falling a few times, he was only greeted by a large stone.
"I guess the elder was right, there is only stone waiting for me here."
Kent moved closer, and while he was praying in his head for the stone to be some treasure that the sect had never known, upon getting close, he saw it was just an ordinary stone.
"Well, what was I expecting anyway?" Kent chuckled, tapping the surface of the stone.
⟦There are markings on it, master, and they seem to be the source of the sword energy.⟧
"You can analyse the markings, Tower, but I am sure these markings were left by a swordsman who was frustrated like I am now."
⟦I will analyse it anyways⟧

chapters.title: Chapter 835: Markings on a Stone [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Peak of the Abandoned Mountain – Kent’s POV]
Kent walked back, sat down, and started to stare at the giant stone.
It had a brown color with a mixture of red and black.
The surface looked polished, like someone had meticulously spent a great deal of time polishing it. That part was strange, and it caught Kent’s attention.

He examined it using his divine senses, but regardless of what he thought, the outcome remained obvious before his eyes: the stone was just an ordinary stone that happened to have a rather classic color combination and a well-polished surface.
Then there were the markings.
Those, too, were but mere markings to Kent.
There were fourteen of them, and each had a different length, depth, and shape. None had anything in common for Kent to take as a point of reference.
In a way, they were mere markings made by a swordsman, no doubt.
Perhaps they were bored and chose to tap into their hidden art talent.
Safe to say they failed cruelly. There was no distinction in the markings at all.
However, Kent couldn’t help but wonder about something that immediately captured his attention, making him walk back, sit down, and start to analyze.
"Since a swordsman made the markings and it was the source of the sword energy I sensed, what does that mean?" Kent wondered.

"For me to sense the sword energy from down there was already enough to know it wasn’t ordinary. I may be regarded as a once-in-a-lifetime genius, but even I can’t leave a mark that will radiate sword energy all the way down there, not even a sword emperor can do that.
This means the markings were made by someone extraordinary."
This conclusion only raised more questions for Kent.
"If this person was extraordinary, why leave markings in a stone and, most importantly, is there even anyone that impressive in this medium world?"
"That elder did say this mountain was abandoned 15 thousand years ago; that was ten thousand years after the Ancient Battle of Parting.
This also means even if these markings were left long before the Parting happened and the limit was placed on this world, nobody back then could have made these markings."
Because of Kent’s deeper understanding of the sword, thanks to Jest, his incarnation, he knew what went into what he had just sensed.
Sword energy is a combination of sword intent and sword aura.
It is difficult to improve, especially from the profound stage upward, and for one to be able to leave such a mark, then it must certainly be someone who has already reached the Sword Immortal stage.
Anyone below that stage wouldn’t be able to even have a shot at leaving their sword energy behind for a year, let alone being sensed from several kilometers away.
"Makes me wonder whether this is something profound or I am just wasting my time, overthinking everything."
Kent took a big sigh but continued to try to make sense of the markings.
After a while, the tower completed its analysis.
⟦I have analyzed every mark, and from what I gathered, these markings are more than 30 thousand years old. Also, they are not made from a sword, but from a sword aura.⟧
"Well, that took a turn quickly." Kent’s interest was piqued, so he started to listen. And well, the tower can now speak, so he wasn’t reading.
Talk about growth and progression.
The tower has graduated and can now speak in a human tone.
⟦I couldn’t accurately estimate the grade of the sword aura, but from the other signs I have seen, it is no less than an Immortal grade.
But here is the strange part: the markings are not random. Inside each marking is a complex technique designed to enhance one’s sword energy (Aura/Intent).
Of course, I will need more time to gain a better understanding of the techniques, but from what I have gathered, this marking contains a technique to attain Perfect Sword Energy.⟧.
Kent furrowed his brow.
"When you say perfect, are we speaking of gaining perfect sword aura and intent in the sense that I will gain the recognition of the sword Dao?"
⟦Yes, master. I am not 100% sure, but from the little I could gather, the technique is aimed at attaining perfect sword aura and sword intent.⟧
Kent stood up, a smile playing on his face as he moved closer to the markings and started scrutinizing them, this time, with more attention to detail.
After a few minutes, he took a few steps back, and his smile turned into laughter.
"Finally, after hundreds of years of searching, who would have thought I would find it in a mere medium world such as this?"
Kent was darn happy.
This technique was one Jest had always had at the back of his mind and had looked for in many worlds before ascending to an immortal world.
Kent had yet to recall his life in the immortal world.

Still, he knew all about his life before ascending, and back then, aside from looking for many ways to grow in his sword path, he had also been looking for one of the fourteen techniques in cultivating perfect sword energy.
"With this, I will be taking a different step toward walking the perfect sword path also." His heart was beating rather fast as he imagined where this was going.
"Perfect sword aura, intent, body, gaze. If I manage to perfect all this before reaching the peak of the sword path, will I then see the path beyond?"
Kent’s ambitions burned much brighter than he could handle at the moment. But he knew what this meant, and that alone was all he could aim for.
"Tower, analyse everything down to the last root and let me know all I need to know."
⟦I will, master⟧
The tower used two good hours to analyze the 14 marks more closely before giving Kent the answer he had been waiting for.
⟦The secrets of this mark are hidden beyond my reach. The master would have to understand them himself⟧
"I expected that, but hearing it stung. In any case, just take the stone into the sword tower," Kent said with a sigh.
⟦I can’t do that, master⟧
"Why?"
⟦Because the moment I take this stone, the whole mountain will come down. Additionally, I cannot take the entire mountain, as that would be too obvious.⟧
"Well, that is just too great. Then the only thing now is to study it using the time of this world."
⟦That is indeed correct. The master must learn to cultivate on the outside too, since in the future, not everything can be used through the tower⟧
Kent just laughed, knowing what the tower said was indeed true. It cannot provide everything, and also can’t take everything inside.
At most, it can only copy some things if there is not enough time to study them. Even so, there is a case where it cannot copy. When that happens, he would have to stay on the outside and study it.
Today was one of those days. He must use the limited time he has at hand to gain a deeper understanding of what the markings conceal beneath.
"I’d better start early." Thus, Kent sat down and began to comprehend the 14 markings.

He examined it using his divine senses, but regardless of what he thought, the outcome remained obvious before his eyes: the stone was just an ordinary stone that happened to have a rather classic color combination and a well-polished surface.
Then there were the markings.
Those, too, were but mere markings to Kent.
There were fourteen of them, and each had a different length, depth, and shape.
None had anything in common for Kent to take as a point of reference.
In a way, they were mere markings made by a swordsman, no doubt.
Perhaps they were bored and chose to tap into their hidden art talent.
Safe to say they failed cruelly.
There was no distinction in the markings at all.
However, Kent couldn’t help but wonder about something that immediately captured his attention, making him walk back, sit down, and start to analyze.
"Since a swordsman made the markings and it was the source of the sword energy I sensed, what does that mean?" Kent wondered.
"For me to sense the sword energy from down there was already enough to know it wasn’t ordinary.
I may be regarded as a once-in-a-lifetime genius, but even I can’t leave a mark that will radiate sword energy all the way down there, not even a sword emperor can do that.
This means the markings were made by someone extraordinary."
This conclusion only raised more questions for Kent.
"If this person was extraordinary, why leave markings in a stone and, most importantly, is there even anyone that impressive in this medium world?"
"That elder did say this mountain was abandoned 15 thousand years ago; that was ten thousand years after the Ancient Battle of Parting.
This also means even if these markings were left long before the Parting happened and the limit was placed on this world, nobody back then could have made these markings."
Because of Kent’s deeper understanding of the sword, thanks to Jest, his incarnation, he knew what went into what he had just sensed.
Sword energy is a combination of sword intent and sword aura.
It is difficult to improve, especially from the profound stage upward, and for one to be able to leave such a mark, then it must certainly be someone who has already reached the Sword Immortal stage.
Anyone below that stage wouldn’t be able to even have a shot at leaving their sword energy behind for a year, let alone being sensed from several kilometers away.
"Makes me wonder whether this is something profound or I am just wasting my time, overthinking everything."
Kent took a big sigh but continued to try to make sense of the markings.
After a while, the tower completed its analysis.
⟦I have analyzed every mark, and from what I gathered, these markings are more than 30 thousand years old.
Also, they are not made from a sword, but from a sword aura.⟧
"Well, that took a turn quickly." Kent’s interest was piqued, so he started to listen.
And well, the tower can now speak, so he wasn’t reading.
Talk about growth and progression.
The tower has graduated and can now speak in a human tone.
⟦I couldn’t accurately estimate the grade of the sword aura, but from the other signs I have seen, it is no less than an Immortal grade.
But here is the strange part: the markings are not random.
Inside each marking is a complex technique designed to enhance one’s sword energy (Aura/Intent).
Of course, I will need more time to gain a better understanding of the techniques, but from what I have gathered, this marking contains a technique to attain Perfect Sword Energy.⟧.
Kent furrowed his brow.
"When you say perfect, are we speaking of gaining perfect sword aura and intent in the sense that I will gain the recognition of the sword Dao?"
⟦Yes, master.
I am not 100% sure, but from the little I could gather, the technique is aimed at attaining perfect sword aura and sword intent.⟧
Kent stood up, a smile playing on his face as he moved closer to the markings and started scrutinizing them, this time, with more attention to detail.
After a few minutes, he took a few steps back, and his smile turned into laughter.
"Finally, after hundreds of years of searching, who would have thought I would find it in a mere medium world such as this?"
Kent was darn happy.
This technique was one Jest had always had at the back of his mind and had looked for in many worlds before ascending to an immortal world.
Kent had yet to recall his life in the immortal world.

Still, he knew all about his life before ascending, and back then, aside from looking for many ways to grow in his sword path, he had also been looking for one of the fourteen techniques in cultivating perfect sword energy.
"With this, I will be taking a different step toward walking the perfect sword path also." His heart was beating rather fast as he imagined where this was going.
"Perfect sword aura, intent, body, gaze.
If I manage to perfect all this before reaching the peak of the sword path, will I then see the path beyond?"
Kent’s ambitions burned much brighter than he could handle at the moment.
But he knew what this meant, and that alone was all he could aim for.
"Tower, analyse everything down to the last root and let me know all I need to know."
⟦I will, master⟧
The tower used two good hours to analyze the 14 marks more closely before giving Kent the answer he had been waiting for.
⟦The secrets of this mark are hidden beyond my reach.
The master would have to understand them himself⟧
"I expected that, but hearing it stung.
In any case, just take the stone into the sword tower," Kent said with a sigh.
⟦I can’t do that, master⟧
"Why?"
⟦Because the moment I take this stone, the whole mountain will come down.
Additionally, I cannot take the entire mountain, as that would be too obvious.⟧
"Well, that is just too great.
Then the only thing now is to study it using the time of this world."
⟦That is indeed correct.
The master must learn to cultivate on the outside too, since in the future, not everything can be used through the tower⟧
Kent just laughed, knowing what the tower said was indeed true.
It cannot provide everything, and also can’t take everything inside.
At most, it can only copy some things if there is not enough time to study them.
Even so, there is a case where it cannot copy.
When that happens, he would have to stay on the outside and study it.
Today was one of those days.
He must use the limited time he has at hand to gain a deeper understanding of what the markings conceal beneath.
"I’d better start early." Thus, Kent sat down and began to comprehend the 14 markings.

chapters.title: Chapter 836 - 834 - Evil Bat is Dead
paragraphs: Kent was hard at work, comprehending the hidden secrets behind the 14 markings.
He remained seated, pouring all his attention into the markings, and using the sword mind, he was doing all he could to understand what was hidden, even from the tower.
Judging by the complexity of the markings, he might need a couple of days, perhaps even weeks, to gain an understanding.
[Human Continent - Evil Sect]
It has already been over two years since Kent’s battle with the evil bat.
Back then, Kent came close to losing, as the gap in cultivation base and strength between him and Evil Bat was too vast.
However, Kent managed to gain the upper hand, and the outcome was more shocking than anyone who witnessed that battle expected.
Kent used a talisman, one that mirrors the life of a person, creates a copy of them, and links them together with the intention of making them enemies.
Evil Bat was pitted against his own image, and the outcome was just too terrifying.
He had to run and hide, and for the past two years, he had remained hidden, hoping that his mirror antagonist would abandon him.
Then once that happened, he could come out of seclusion and handle the brat who had sent him into hiding in the first place.
His sect poured all their resources into helping him grow much stronger.
Just a few hours ago, Evil Bat has finally managed to break into the Core Formation stage, bringing him the confidence he has lost over the past 2 years.
He remained hidden in his secret underground chamber, doing his best to gain control over his energy before he steps out.
A couple of hours later, when he finally did, his body exploded with energy.
"Kent Madson, wait for your death," he muttered, looking coldly at the stone wall.
Suddenly, an elder, looking more bony than bones themselves, appeared in hurried steps, kneeling before Evil Bat.
"Congratulations, sect leader."
"Drop the flattery and tell me, have you located the clone?"
"No, sect leader. At first, it was living in the mountains, but for a while now, we haven’t sensed even a trace of it anywhere, at least not anywhere within a 3,000-mile radius of the sect.
I think it had run out of energy and probably dissipated."
Evil Bat didn’t say anything; instead, he unleashed his senses, covering several thousand miles in search of the clone. However, no matter how hard he looked, the clone was nowhere to be found.
"I suppose you are right. After all, it was a clone created using runes." He stood up, and while he didn’t make it obvious, the elder could see the nervous look on his face.
But as someone who values his life, he said nothing.
"Anything else I should know?" Evil Bat asked.
"Nothing too important, sect leader. However, two years ago, after your battle with Kent, the other sects attacked us using your absence as their fuel.
Many died, but in the end, we managed to repel them. We fed their bodies to the beast, and now that you are stronger than ever, I believe we can get our revenge."
Evil Bat didn’t say anything but just vanished away and then appeared above ground. The moment he breathed the fresh air, he felt a pair of eyes locked onto him.
Then it came, crashing down on him.
When he turned and looked, he saw an identical copy of himself lunging at him.
"What?"
His eyes widened with shock as he braced for impact.
BOOM
The clone landed a powerful punch on the Evil Bat’s crossed arm, breaking the bones.
"Aaarrgghhh!"
The pain shot through Evil Bat’s arm like wildfire, like hellish flames licking at his broken bones.
This disturbance immediately drew the attention of the elders, causing them to surround the clone.
However, before any of them could attack, the clone waved its hand, and their bodies exploded, turning into bats.
This only added to Evil Bat’s pain. He gritted his teeth and staggered backward, barely managing to keep his footing.
From the attacks that broke his arm to witnessing 10 elders blown up, he realized he had done nothing in the past 2 years.
The only thing he accomplished was strengthening the clone to not only end his life but also destroy the sect in the process.
Kent told him that as he grew stronger, so would the clone. However, he didn’t believe him, thinking he was merely trying to scare him into fighting the clone to the death back then.
But now, he saw that Kent didn’t mess with him, that he had doomed himself, or more like he was doomed from the start.
The clone pressed the advantage without hesitation, a cruel smile twisting its lips.
Though it can’t talk, the expression on its face probably said something along the lines of "You’re weaker than I thought," it sneered.
Evil Bat growled and summoned every ounce of his Core Formation energy, igniting his other arm in a swirling aura of dark flame. "I won’t lose... not this time!"

He swung with brutal force, aiming a devastating strike at the clone’s chest. But the clone was faster, effortlessly dodging and retaliating with a series of rapid punches that battered Evil Bat’s ribs.
Blood spilled from his mouth, and his vision blurred, but he forced himself to stand firm.
The clone is identical to Evil Bat, but without his weaknesses and flaws. So naturally, Kent has created a perfect battle companion for Evil Bat, only that this one aims to take his life.

Evil Bat tried to block, but the clone’s palm slammed into his chest with the force of a mountain. His body flew backward, crashing through trees and smashing into the ground hard enough to crack the earth beneath him.
Half the sect was destroyed from that one’s attack, and more than 300 Evil Sect disciples perished.
Struggling to breathe, Evil Bat crawled to his feet. His strength was fading fast. The clone approached, cold and merciless.

With a final roar, Evil Bat gathered his remaining energy for one last desperate attack. But before he could strike, the clone’s shadow stretched out, wrapping around him like chains forged from darkness.
The pressure crushed him, breaking bones, squeezing the life from his lungs.
His bones shattered, creating a sickening sound.
Evil Bat’s eyes glazed over. He tried to scream, but no sound came.
Blood fell from his eyes, nose, ears, and mouth as the clone’s shadow tightened the binding around Evil Bat’s body.
Evil Bat’s body went limp.𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶
The clone released him, letting the lifeless corpse slump to the ground.
Evil Bat had yet to shuffle off the mortal coil; however, he wasn’t far from that junction.
In the few seconds before he died, he activated something.
The battle was soon over.
Evil Bat was dead, and the clone vanished as well.
However, a few seconds later, a sealed door was opened, and a giant lion beast appeared, radiating a rather sinister energy.
In Evil Bat’s bid to get revenge on the clone, he forgot one thing Kent said that day.
He and the clone are linked, so the moment he died, the clone also died, meaning releasing the beast was the end for his sect.
In under 20 minutes, those who couldn’t run fast enough were killed.
Then the panther turned its gaze to the rest of the human kingdoms.
However, it didn’t get the chance, for Elder Lance, who witnessed the entire battle, intervened and killed the panther a few exchanges later.
"Using a mirror clone to kill your enemy, just what kind of monster are you, Kent Madson?" Elder Lance wondered, staring at the destroyed sect.
A few seconds later, he left.

chapters.title: Chapter 837: Remembering Him
paragraphs: [Planet Kryos (Immortal World). Nebulon Mountain. Grand Pyris Pagoda – Last Floor. 20 days later]

Currently, seated inside her jade throne, on the last floor of the Grand Pyris Pagoda in the immortal world, Pill Immortal Nefeli, one of the best alchemists in the universe, seems to be in deep thought.
In her hand is a sketched image, one that seems to have been drawn from bits and pieces of her memory. While the picture appears good and human, it still lacks some elements.
However, it is a picture of Kent, one that can be used to identify him.
The past couple of days saw Pill Immortal Nefeli recalling things from her past that she had never known she had in her mind.

She, at points, out of nowhere, will blackout, sometimes for a couple of minutes, sometimes for a few seconds. Though recently, she doesn’t black out anymore, but out of nowhere, a memory will appear in her mind.
"Kent, the one who joined the Alliance with just a Pill Grandmaster status, and I was even the one who added him. What was I thinking, adding mere grandmaster to the alliance?"
That was the first memory that came to her after the initial awakening 20 days ago. She was confused to think she had added someone so low in the path of the pill to the alliance filled with talents.
Of course, while her initial shock was due to her limited memories, a few days later, she realized why she had done that.
"To think a mere Pill Grandmaster was able to tell a Tier 12 pill from Tier 9 ingredients, now I understand why I added him.
I would have killed to get someone like that on my side."
This memory made her happy, which only got even more interesting as more memories started pouring in.
A few days after the third memory, she remembered how, during the duel between Pill King Han Lu and Pill King Yota, Kent was paying attention to their every movement.
It was something that caught her attention.
This only deepened her image of Kent, and while it had been hundreds of thousands of years already, his image was slowly returning to her.
Then, there was the memory of when Kent gave her the Soul-type recipes.
Just like how she felt when Kent gave her the recipes, her mind was blown away this time, too.
Because of those memories, she had been pondering the fact that she finally knew where all the recipes came from.
"He gave me 20 Soul-type pill recipes like it was nothing." This memory served as a wake-up call for her to delve deeper into learning more about Kent.
Of course, the first thing she did was return to the Pyris Pill world, which had now become the top Pill world among the ten Pill worlds.
When she checked the contribution chart, she found out Kent’s name had made two contributions, each a Soul-type pill.
She checked how the contribution was made, and that was when she discovered that she was the one who had collected the contribution and recorded it.
It was a moment of shock to her, and while she didn’t want to draw too much attention, she followed up on the next memory, and that led her to Pill Immortal Suoh, the heavenly Pill Immortal.
It was there she learned that Pill Immortal Suoh was also going through the same thing.
Of course, they knew each other thanks to Kent.
It was after a few days that she realized their friendship had blossomed because of their shared connection to Kent. This made them start to question many things again.
To get more answers, she drew Kent’s image to the best of her ability, intending to use her secret connections to find out who this Kent was.
"No matter what, I must look for him."
[40 days later - Pill Immortal Nefeli’s Immortal Garden]
Pill Immortal Nefeli was painting the 99th image of Kent when suddenly, somebody rushed into her immortal garden.
"My lady, something big has happened."
She paused her painting and set the brush down.
"Yuna, one of these days, I am going to seal your body and turn you into a puppet. How many times did I tell you to walk and not run when entering the garden?"
Yuna, a dark-haired beauty with an aura of a Root Immortal, smiled.
"I am sorry, my lady, I just couldn’t contain my happiness and shock."
Pill Immortal Nefeli turned and looked at her, "You are always happy."
"This time I am overly happy."
Pill Immortal Nefeli just smirked, "Tell me why you are happy then."
"You won’t believe it, but I just got word that the Sword Dao Tablet has just inscribed a name. I have never heard that name before, but everyone is talking about this mysterious name."
"Are you going to tell me the name, or should I pull it out of your mouth?"
Yuna smiled, "The name that appeared on the tablet is Kent Madson, an unknown person."
"What did you just say?" Pill Immortal Nefeli appeared before Yuna, looking very demanding.
Yuna didn’t panic, for she knew her master wouldn’t hurt her. To anyone other than her, they would have panicked and fled.𝘧𝓇ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝘣𝓃ℴ𝓋𝑒𝑙.𝑐𝘰𝑚
To her, seeing her master this eager to hear something and even displaying these many expressions made her happy.
Her master is always cold and distant, so this was a new side of her she would love to see more often. Her master has shown her an emotion, which means she wasn’t a robot, as most thought she was.
"I haven’t seen the name myself, but from rumors going around, the name Kent Madson has appeared on the Sword Dao Tablet.
Many sword Sovereigns and immortals are already making their way to the Sword Canyon to look at it themselves. This is big, which means...
"The sword world is about to become more interesting and deadly again," Pill Immortal Nefeli smiled.
"Why are you smiling?" Yuna asked, looking strangely at her master.
Pill Immortal Nefeli looked at the half-completed image of the handsome purple-haired brat on her canvas, and her smile bloomed.
"I will be away for a while, Yuna. Be sure to look after yourself and don’t get into a fight with the others. I know you are the strongest, so don’t bully them."
"I will, master," Yuna smiled, "And don’t worry, I will take care of the garden, making sure all the flowers are nurtured."
"Just don’t kill them."
Saying that, Pill Immortal Nefeli vanished. Yuna looked at the image of the person on her master’s canvas and smiled.
"If you turn out to be a scam and you break her heart, I will gut you, whoever you are or whatever your name is."
She also left, leaving the canvas behind.
A few minutes after they left, an ethereal beauty, one whose beauty is out of this world, appeared in front of the canvas and formed a chair out of nothing and sat down.
She gazed intently at the half-completed image on the canvas, spending several hours just staring at it like she wanted to burn it into her head.
After a day, she used her hand to brush Kent’s cheek and stood up.
"Looks like you are back, Jest, and have already started making waves. As expected of the Genesis himself," she smiled.
"But for abandoning me, I will gut you when I get my hands on you... punk." Her divine aura leaked, which drew Yuna’s attention. However, by the time she arrived, the lady was already gone.
"Maybe I miss my master so much that I thought she had returned."
